chief_complaint: severe boring epigastric pain radiating to back and vomiting after alcohol
hpi_details: A 38-year-old female presents to the clinic with severe boring epigastric pain radiating to back and vomiting after alcohol. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks drinking alcohol at dinner triggered an acute gallbladder spasm or that repeated vomiting tore her stomach lining.
concerns: She is worried that an internal organ has ruptured and that being hospitalized will leave her unable to arrange care for her two young children.
expectations: She hopes to receive immediate IV medication to take away the agonizing pain and stop the vomiting.

investigation_events.title: STAT acute pancreatitis laboratory results
investigation_events.availability_message: The STAT acute pancreatitis laboratory results are now available; analgesia and goal-directed fluid resuscitation should not be delayed.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Acute Pancreatitis is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Initial management includes analgesia and goal-directed isotonic crystalloid resuscitation, preferably lactated Ringer's solution; begin oral feeding as tolerated rather than maintaining routine prolonged NPO status.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: severe boring epigastric pain radiating to back and vomiting after alcohol

Key HPI features: A 38-year-old female presents to the clinic with severe boring epigastric pain radiating to back and vomiting after alcohol. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Acute Pancreatitis.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Acute Pancreatitis.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Peptic ulcer perforation without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Repeated vomiting with severe pain unrelieved by position — risk of severe pancreatitis.
management_principles: Provide analgesia and goal-directed lactated Ringer's resuscitation; begin oral feeding as tolerated and assess severity and cause
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with chief complaint of severe boring epigastric pain radiating to back and vomiting after alcohol. HPI: alcohol intake, hypertriglyceridemia.
reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Acute Pancreatitis.
reference_soap.assessment: Condition highly suspicious for Acute Pancreatitis.
reference_soap.plan: Confirm the diagnosis and assess severity and etiology. Provide analgesia and goal-directed lactated Ringer's resuscitation while monitoring for fluid overload. Start oral feeding as tolerated rather than routine prolonged NPO status; reserve enteral tube feeding for patients unable to eat.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Acute Pancreatitis
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Acute Pancreatitis
Implement evidence-based management plan: goal-directed fluids, analgesia, early feeding as tolerated, and severity assessment

teaching.one_liner: The pancreas becomes acutely inflamed, most often from alcohol or gallstones, causing severe boring epigastric pain that radiates to the back with repeated vomiting.
red_flags: Repeated vomiting with severe pain unrelieved by position — risk of severe pancreatitis

must_ask.say: Does the pain go through to your spine or the middle of your back?
Did you drink a lot of alcohol before this started?
Have you ever been told you have gallstones?
Does leaning forward or curling up ease the pain at all?
Have you been told your triglycerides or fats in the blood are high?

history.answer: I have this unbearable, constant pain high in my stomach that cuts straight through to my back, and I've been throwing up repeatedly since drinking last night.
It started about twelve hours ago, a few hours after I finished drinking, and it quickly built up into this relentless, severe ache.
The pain is centered right in the middle of my upper belly under my breastbone, and it hasn't shifted anywhere else.
Yes, it shoots straight through my upper belly into my spine and mid-back like a spike.
It feels like a deep, boring, heavy pressure that never lets up, rather than cramps that come and go.
Right now it is an eight or nine out of ten; it's the most severe pain I have ever felt.
Lying flat on my back makes the pain much worse, but curling into a ball and leaning forward eases it just a little.
No, I have never had an episode of severe belly pain like this in my life.
I have thrown up four or five times already, mostly clear liquid and bitter yellowish bile, but no blood or coffee-ground material.
I passed gas this morning, but I haven't moved my bowels since yesterday; no diarrhea, black tarry stool, or blood.
I felt flushed and sweaty from the pain, but I haven't had shaking chills or a high fever.
No, my skin and the whites of my eyes look normal, my urine isn't dark brown, and my bowel movements haven't been pale.
No burning or pain when I pee, no increased frequency, and no blood in my urine.
I feel exhausted, washed out, and slightly lightheaded when I stand up, but I haven't fainted.
No, I don't have any vaginal bleeding, spotting, or unusual discharge.
No chest pressure, chest tightness, or trouble breathing, though taking a very deep breath hurts because of my belly.
Last night I drank about a whole bottle of wine and ate fried greasy pork at a get-together with my coworkers.
I took two acetaminophen tablets early this morning, but they didn't help at all; I haven't taken any ibuprofen, aspirin, or other painkillers.
No, I have never had any heart rhythm issues, palpitations, or vascular problems.
No, an ultrasound during my routine checkup two years ago showed no stones or problems in my gallbladder.
At my company health checkup six months ago, the doctor noted that my triglycerides were quite high and told me to cut back on fatty food.
I thought maybe having drinks at dinner triggered an acute gallbladder spasm or that vomiting so hard tore my stomach lining.
The pain goes straight through to my back and I'm terrified something ruptured inside and I'll be stuck in the hospital with nobody to watch my young kids.
I just desperately need some strong IV medicine to stop this unbearable pain and nausea so I can think straight.
I don't have high blood pressure, diabetes, or any other chronic medical conditions besides the borderline high triglycerides.
I have never had any surgeries or stays in the hospital.
I do not take any daily prescription medicines, over-the-counter drugs, or herbal remedies.
I have no known allergies to medications, foods, or anything else.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I usually only drink one or two glasses of wine a month socially, but yesterday was a special dinner so I drank far more than usual.
I work as an accountant in an office and live with my husband in an apartment.
My parents are in their sixties and healthy, and nobody in my family has had pancreatitis, gallstones, or GI cancer.
My last period started two weeks ago and was normal, my cycle is 28 days, my husband uses condoms, and there is no chance I am pregnant.

exam.finding: Patient appears acutely ill, grimacing with discomfort and sitting upright while leaning slightly forward.
Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, pulse 104 beats/min, respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, temperature 37.3°C, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Conjunctivae are pink without pallor, and sclerae are clear without jaundice or icterus.
Abdomen is mildly distended with no surgical scars, caput medusae, or Cullen or Grey Turner signs.
Hypoactive bowel sounds across all quadrants; no abdominal bruits heard.
Severe tenderness on deep palpation in the epigastric region without rigid involuntary guarding.
No rebound tenderness elicited in any quadrant.
Negative Murphy's sign with no inspiratory arrest upon deep palpation of the right upper quadrant.
No tenderness at McBurney's point; psoas and obturator signs are negative.
Normal sphincter tone, no palpable mass or tenderness, and brown stool on glove with negative occult blood.
